title: Permutations and Combinations
seo_title: Permutations and Combinations – SSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Use factorials; count arrangements (permutations) and selections (combinations); use them to find probabilities. (summary of the NERDC SSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 maths worksheets on permutations and combinations: factorials, nPr, nCr, the counting principle and probability. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • n! = n × (n − 1) × … × 2 × 1.
  • ⁿPᵣ = n! ÷ (n − r)! counts arrangements where order matters.
  • ⁿCᵣ = n! ÷ (r!(n − r)!) counts selections where order does not matter.

Examples

Example

Choose 2 prefects from 5 pupils

⁵C₂ = 5 × 4 ÷ 2

Answer: 10 ways

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using a permutation for a committeeA committee is a combination.
Thinking 0! = 00! = 1.
Adding instead of multiplying choicesMultiply the choices at each stage.

A committee of 4 is chosen at random from 9 people, including Hauwa and Samuel. What is the probability that both Hauwa and Samuel are chosen?
items.e: Ways that include both: 7C2 = 21. All committees: 9C4 = 126. 21/126 = 16.

items.q: 6 books, including a dictionary and an atlas, are placed on a shelf in random order. What is the probability that the dictionary is first and the atlas is second?
items.e: Arrangements with those two fixed: 4! = 24. All arrangements: 6! = 720. 130.
